# Copilot Instructions for homebrew-tap

## What this repo is

A [Homebrew tap](https://docs.brew.sh/Taps) — a `brew tap l337-org/tap` source, nothing else. It
holds only `Formula/*.rb` and this repo's own docs; there is no application code, no CI, and (as
of this file) no build pipeline defined *in this repo*. Formulae are consumed with
`brew install l337-org/tap/<name>`.

## How a formula gets here

Each formula is generated by its upstream project's own release pipeline, not written by hand
here. Today that's `docker-mcp-server`: `Formula/docker-mcp-server.rb` is rendered from
`scripts/docker-mcp-server.rb.tpl` in [L337-org/docker-mcp](https://github.com/L337-org/docker-mcp)
by that repo's `publish-homebrew.yaml` workflow on each GitHub Release, and pushed here as a commit
authored by `github-actions[bot]`. **Don't hand-edit a generated formula** — a manual change is
silently overwritten by the next automated push, and it puts this repo's copy out of sync with the
template that regenerates it. If a formula needs to change, change the template upstream and let
the workflow push the result; a hand-edit is only a stopgap for validating a fix before it's rolled
into the template (see the caveat below for the one case where that happened).

## `docker-mcp-server` formula — what it installs and why it looks like this

Installs the [docker-mcp-server](https://github.com/L337-org/docker-mcp) MCP server. Because the
formula is a `uv venv` + `uv pip install --no-index --find-links=...` from a pre-built "wheelhouse"
tarball (attached to the matching GitHub Release) rather than a source build, `depends_on "uv" =>
:build` is present purely to create the venv; there's no compilation step of our own. `bin.install_symlink`
exposes both console entry points (`docker-mcp-server` and `docker-mcp`) matching the package's
own dual-name convention.

`skip_clean "libexec"` (added by hand, see caveat below) tells Homebrew's post-install **cleanup**
phase (stripping symbols, pruning `.la` files, etc.) to leave the venv alone — it does not by
itself disable the separate keg-relocation step that rewrites dylib IDs via `install_name_tool`.
Whether skipping cleanup on `libexec` is actually sufficient to route around the header-padding
failure described below is exactly the part that's unverified — see the caveat.

**Caveat — stale and mid-fix.** This formula currently sits at `v1.9.2` and still names the
pre-org-migration repo (`GavinLucas/docker-mcp`, not `L337-org/docker-mcp`) because
`publish-homebrew.yaml`'s release trigger has been disabled (`workflow_dispatch`-only) since before
the org move, pending confirmation of a real fix for a Homebrew dylib-linkage failure: pre-built
`pydantic_core` wheels lack `-headerpad_max_install_names`, so Homebrew's relocation step fails to
rewrite the `@rpath` ID on install. `skip_clean "libexec"` above was added directly to this repo's
copy (commit `53b5c8e`, June 2026) as a candidate fix, ahead of and outside the normal
template→workflow→push path — it has **not** been round-tripped into `docker-mcp`'s template, and
the channel is still paused, so treat it as unverified rather than as evidence the issue is closed.
Don't "helpfully" refresh this formula to the current version or org name by hand; that's the
generator's job once the channel is re-enabled upstream. If you're looking into re-enabling the
channel, start in `docker-mcp`'s CLAUDE.md ("Homebrew tap" section) and `publish-homebrew.yaml`, not
here.

## Updating a formula / testing expectations

Normal path: land the fix in `docker-mcp`'s `scripts/docker-mcp-server.rb.tpl`, cut a release there,
and let `publish-homebrew.yaml` push the regenerated formula here — nothing to do in this repo.

If you do need to touch a formula directly in this repo (e.g. a hand-verified stopgap like the
`skip_clean` line above), test it before pushing:

```bash
brew install --build-from-source ./Formula/<name>.rb   # or without --build-from-source if it fetches a prebuilt asset
brew test <name>
brew audit --strict --online ./Formula/<name>.rb
```

`brew test` runs the formula's own `test do` block (e.g. `docker-mcp-server`'s `import docker_mcp`
smoke check) — confirm it passes on the platform(s) the change targets before pushing, since there
is no CI here to catch a regression.

## Ownership

`.github/CODEOWNERS` gates every change on review from `@GavinLucas` — there's no other automated
gate in this repo, so that review is the only check a change gets.
